evidence: Hang Tre Street, or Phố Hàng Tre in Vietnamese, is a vibrant and bustling thoroughfare situated along the winding dike road of the Red River, on the edge of Hanoi's Old Quarter. This historic street has been a hub of activity since the time when bamboo rafts, luong, and nua from upstream regions flowed downstream to supply building materials for the entire imperial city.

Today, the street remains a popular gathering spot for locals and tourists alike, with a series of restaurants and eateries packed closely together. The street's unique identifying feature is the imposing concrete dike wall stretching along one side, enclosing the road and creating a sense of enclosure.
